page: OVHcloud i1-90 is a storage-optimized virtual instance configured on KVM hypervisor architecture. The instance provides 16 dedicated physical x86_64 cores running at 2.2 GHz using Intel Haswell generation hardware without hyperthreading. It includes 90 GB of system memory, providing 5.62 GB of RAM per core, backed by 16 MB of L3 cache. For local data persistence, the instance features a combined 3850 GB NVMe SSD volume consisting of 3800 GB primary NVMe storage and a 50 GB system SSD. Baseline network throughput is configured at 2 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear contrast between single-core throughput and multi-threaded scaling. Single-core performance falls into the lower tier across tests, scoring 923.0 in Geekbench and 1028.7 in stress-ng single-core suites. Single-threaded compression also reflects this limitation, with gzip reaching 16.98 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 6.65 GB/sec. In contrast, the absence of hyperthreading across 16 fully dedicated physical cores brings multi-threaded performance into the middle tier, yielding a multi-core Geekbench score of 7335.0, a PassMark CPU score of 20190.37, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression of 94.13 GB/sec.

Memory bandwidth measurements demonstrate mid-tier throughput, showing 93.93 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 43.32 GB/sec for large block writes. In transactional and operational testing, the instance delivered 22.17 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 13.75 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. CPU-based machine learning inference is restricted by the older architecture, with text generation on a 7B model recording 7.51 tokens per second.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the instance maximizes resource density around its 3850 GB local NVMe array and 90 GB memory allocation. The primary trade-off involves subdued per-thread execution speeds compared to modern architectures. Consequently, the OVHcloud i1-90 is well aligned for storage-heavy services, clustered database engines, caching layers, log aggregation nodes, and parallel ETL batch processing that rely on dedicated physical cores and local disk capacity.
description: OVHcloud i1-90 is a storage-optimized cloud instance providing 16 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Haswell x86_64 architecture clocked at 2.2 GHz. The hardware package bundles 90 GB of RAM and 3850 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, supplemented by a 2 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark telemetry highlights average multi-core processing capability, scoring 20190.37 on PassMark CPU and 7335.0 on Geekbench multi-core, offset by lower single-threaded metrics due to legacy core clock speeds. Memory throughput remains balanced, producing 93.93 GB/sec on large read blocks and achieving 22.17 million operations per second on Redis SET workloads. Because it trades single-thread compute efficiency for dedicated physical cores and expansive local high-speed disk arrays, this instance is suited for localized database clusters, data caching deployments, log collection systems, and high-capacity batch storage tasks.
